do.name: Pena Palace and park
do.detail: The yellow-and-red Romanticist palace on the ridge; timed entry slots, so book the official Parques de Sintra shop ahead.

do.name: Walk the Moorish Castle ramparts
do.detail: 9th century fortress walls snaking along the hilltop, with the widest views over Sintra and the Atlantic; cars are restricted, walk or bus up.

do.name: Descend the Initiation Well at Quinta da Regaleira
do.detail: Spiral nine storeys down the mossy well, then thread the estate's tunnels, grottoes and symbol-laden gardens.

do.name: Monserrate palace and botanical gardens
do.detail: Mughal-inspired pink villa in exotic gardens, the quiet counterpoint to Pena on the far side of the serra.

do.name: Cabo da Roca and Peninha sanctuary
do.detail: Stand at continental Europe's westernmost cliff, then detour to the Peninha chapel for one of Portugal's finest coastal views.

do.name: National Palace of Sintra
do.detail: The one in the middle of town, under two enormous white kitchen chimneys. Portuguese kings used it for six centuries, and the tiled rooms are the best in the country.

do.name: Hike up through Vila Sassetti to the castles
do.detail: Skip the bus: forest paths climb from the old town past Villa Sassetti to the Moorish Castle and Pena, about 200 m of ascent.

do.name: Tram to Praia das Macas and the wild beaches
do.detail: Ride the 11.5 km heritage tram to Praia das Macas, or seek out Adraga, the Ursa scramble and the ocean pool at Azenhas do Mar.

do.name: Travesseiros and queijadas at Piriquita
do.detail: Warm almond-cream travesseiros at the 1862 Casa Piriquita and cinnamon queijadas, Sintra's two signature pastries.
